title: Ah-SCDFT:A general approach for superconductivity with an-harmonic corrections
authors: Xiaozheng Fan, Panshi Jing, Chuanguang Zhang, Junshuai Wang, Chunlan Ma, Shijing Gong, Chuanxi Zhao, Tianxing Wang, Yipeng An
abstract: First-principles studies of superconductivity often neglect anharmonic effects (AHE), despite their crucial role in achieving quantitative accuracy in many materials. To bridge this gap, we introduce a general computational approach, termed anharmonic superconducting density functional theory (ah-SCDFT) which systematically incorporates anharmonic corrections into standard SCDFT. This approach allows for high-fidelity predictions of superconducting properties with only a modest increase in computational cost for a limited number of superconducting calculation convergence steps. We demonstrate the effectiveness and reliability of ah-SCDFT by applying it to the prototypical superconductor MgB2, accurately reproducing its superconducting behavior under both ambient conditions and applied pressure in excellent agreement with experiment. Our results establish ah-SCDFT as a powerful, efficient, and broadly applicable approach for quantitatively reliable studies of superconductivity and a promising tool for the prediction of new superconducting materials.
summary: This paper introduces ah-SCDFT, a general theoretical framework that incorporates crucial anharmonic lattice vibrations into first-principles calculations for superconductivity. By applying this method to MgB2, the authors demonstrate that including these effects significantly improves the accuracy of predicted superconducting critical temperatures and gaps compared to simpler harmonic approximations.
main_problem: First-principles studies of superconductivity often neglect anharmonic effects (AHE), which are crucial for achieving quantitative accuracy in predicting superconducting properties.
main_result: The proposed ah-SCDFT approach accurately reproduces the experimental superconducting behavior of MgB2 under ambient conditions and applied pressure, resolving theoretical discrepancies regarding Tc(P).
method: The authors introduce anharmonic superconducting density functional theory (ah-SCDFT), which systematically incorporates anharmonic corrections into standard SCDFT by minimizing the Helmholtz free energy.
model_or_system: The study focuses on superconductivity, using the prototypical superconductor MgB2 as a test case. The methodology involves combining first-principles electronic structure calculations with finite-temperature equilibrium structures derived from the quasi-harmonic approximation (QHA).
key_observables: Superconducting critical temperature ($T_c$), superconducting gaps, electron-phonon coupling constant ($\lambda$), and pressure dependence of these quantities.
important_parameters: Temperature (ambient to elevated), applied pressure (up to 200 GPa), and the vibrational free energy terms.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that anharmonic corrections are necessary for reliable quantitative predictions, overcoming limitations inherent in the harmonic approximation.
figures_summary: Figures compare superconducting gaps calculated with and without anharmonicity (Figure 2); they show phonon dispersion and DOS at different temperatures/pressures (Figure 3); and they illustrate pressure dependence of lattice constants and Tc (Figure 4).
paper_structure: The paper establishes the need for anharmonic corrections, details the ah-SCDFT methodology involving iterative free energy minimization, applies it to MgB2 under varying conditions (T and P), and compares results against experimental data.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter superconductivity, the rigorous inclusion of finite-temperature effects via free energy minimization and anharmonic corrections touches upon advanced statistical mechanics treatments of interacting quantum systems.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. (a) General approach for studying superconductivity with incorporated anharmonic effects. T(P) denotes the predicted critical temperature T at a given pressure P, used for the lattice renormalization. (b) Convergent Tc and Tcn under several temperature dependent geometries. The horizontal dashed line marks the final converged Tcn.

FIG. 2. (a) Temperature-dependent superconducting gaps. The superconducting gaps of MgB2 are shown as a function of temperature, comparing anharmonic (red symbols) and harmonic (blue symbols) calculations. Solid, semi-filled, and hollow red circles represent the maximum, average, and minimum superconducting gaps obtained with anharmonic effects, respectively, across the temperature range from 0.1 K to 39 K (Tc). The blue semi-filled circles correspond to the average superconducting gap calculated using the harmonic geometry. (b) Density of states (DOS) of MgB2 calculated using harmonic (blue line, 0 K) and anharmonic (red line, 39 K) equilibrium geometries.

FIG. 3. Phonon and electron-phonon coupling properties of MgB2 within the harmonic approximation (0 K, blue lines) and with the inclusion of anharmonic effects (39 K, red lines). (a) Element-projected phonon dispersion with electron- phonon coupling λqν (purple balls) and phonon linewidth γqν (green balls). (b) Phonon density of states (PhDOS). (c) Frequency-dependent Eliashberg spectral functions α2F(ω) with the cumulative EPC strength λ(ω).

FIG. 4. (a) Pressure-dependent lattice constants including anharmonic effects. (b) Pressure-dependent superconducting critical temperature Tc within the harmonic approximation (blue balls) and with the inclusion of anharmonic effects (red balls), as well as the electron-phonon coupling constant λ for the case of including the anharmonic effects.
